Currently I have only worked in 1:48 scale and 28mm with the few odd 25mm figures. I agree that 28mm is a great scale as it is large enough to have models with good detail yet about the smallest size to not make a 6'x4' table feel too small...mostly. Although, at 28mm, modern weaponry easily out distances the size of the table, but I can live with that concession for the detail of the figures themselves.

I also find that I generally like skirmish to small platoon sized games of at least WWII tech/tactics. I only want larger sized (i.e. company) games to allow for vehicles which I generally prefer to have in my force over infantry given preference. I like games that allow at least of 50/50 mix of vehicles to infantry that has around a 8-12 units to a force in a standard sized game. I think 28mm (or there about) is a good size to meet my wants in a game.

As for painting at the larger scale it doesn't bother me too much. I suspect because it is the only scale I know. I don't mind painting to enjoying it somewhat, though; I really enjoy the finished product. When I started miniatures gaming, I was all about the game. Now, I really like fielding good looking miniatures in addition. I also find I enjoy playing an opponent that has painted their force (especially if they have put some effort into it) more than primer only or bare plastic/metal. Sadly, I don't get in that many games against opponents that bother to paint their stuff. Which I know shouldn't take away from my enjoyment of the game, but it kinda does.

My preference is for 25-50 mm figs and the overwhelming majority of my painting has been in that range. I've done some painting at smaller scales, like Epic but I found that there wasn't enough detail to keep me interested. Even now, I'm starting to have serious eye problems and I have a hard time painting something in the 28-30mm range. Hell I can barely see the eyes on these things now and it's driving me crazy. I haven't had the opportunity to paint larger busts and whatnot but I'm intrigued by the possibility. If only they weren't so outrageously priced.

Why do you think reddit decided to fall on it's own sword by virtue of their new harassment policy? Will Atko ever go down the same road?

Because the new CEO wanted Reddit to be more profitable. She wanted to get out of the way popular subreddits that were seen as "Evil" by the general SJW public and when Imgur started deleting /r/fatpeoplehate's pictures because they were offended (coincidentally the IMGUR admin team is fat), she got scared it might blow up and she couldn't sell advertisement spots anymore.

Sadly Ellen Pao does not seem to understand her own user base and ended up shooting herself in the foot by making Reddit "safer".

Let's examine what has occured so far:

  1. Reddit banned 5 subs, most notably FPH with 150K subscribers and many more lurkers.
  2. Reddit appears to be suppressing free speech as seen with this measure and with recent posts/comments on the site.
  3. FPHaters and other reddit users moved to voat or installed AdBlock and stopped buying reddit gold, in an effort not to support reddit.

Now, there are many, like me admittedly, who are still in a transition stage, using both until voat gets its shit together completely. But I'm trying to create the threads I'm used to seeing on reddit so that Voat becomes my new home. However, is 150K gonna be significant in a site that has millions of subscribers? I doubt it.

What can happen is that reddit continues its trend of suppressing free speech, banning more subreddits and shadowbanning users for no apparent reason, and more people (more importantly sponsors) get tired of it and stop using and supporting reddit. If this trend continues to happen, then I think the answer to your question is yes. I don't know what Atko is.

Also, for this to happen, Voat or an equivalent site needs to be able to support the influx of frustrated exredditors, because they won't leave unless they have another suitable place to settle.
Just on a side note, I think Atko is the username of the guy running Voat. (assuming you meant you didn't recognize the name, rather than saying you were't sure what he'll do)

As several users on reddit have said, Pao appears to be trying to streamline reddit for advertisers. I think Atko will remain pure, but nothing lasts forever. One day, Voat may be bought out by someone else who goes down the path that reddit did. It's the circle of life.
